To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the toxicity of sediment elutriates from Ría de Ponteverdra (Galicia, Spain) is related to the concentrations of metals in sediments and that this correspondence can be used to identify polluted areas in the ria and to predict the harmful ecological effects of sediment contamination.
the toxic effects of sediments from the Ría de Pontvedra can be explained by the presence of metals, especially Cu and Zn, which are the pollutants of concern in these sediments.

the sediment quality guidelines and a toxic unit approach, applied to the results from an integrative assessment, can help to explain the observed toxicity in elutriate embryo- larvae bioassays with Paracentrotus livudus and Ciona intestinalis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a multidisciplinary approach to the assessment of sediment quality in Ría de Pontedera, which may be useful in the management of this coastal area.
the use of sediment chemistry and elutriate toxicity bioassays to identify polluted areas and assess the potential harmful effects of sediment contamination in a coastal system.
a better understanding of how to integrate sediment chemistry and toxicity data to assess the effects of sediment contamination in coastal areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sediment chemistry and toxicity were correlated, and that the most polluted sites were those with the highest toxicity.
the toxicological data obtained from the bioassays are in agreement with the chemistry of the sediments and the results obtained from sediment quality guidelines.

the sediment toxicity observed at the sites P2 and especially at P3 is related to the metal concentrations found in the sediments, and the toxicity at site P3 is mainly attributable to the Cu and Zn contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sediment toxicity in the Ría de Ponteverdra is associated with high concentrations of Cu and Zn.
the sediment chemistry and toxicity profiles were in agreement, and that the toxic unit approach was useful in predicting the ecological effects of sediment pollution.
the combination of sediment chemistry data with embryo-larval toxicity tests is a powerful tool to assess the ecological quality status of coastal systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of sediment quality guidelines and the toxic unit approach can provide a valuable tool to help in the assessment of sediment pollution.
sediment quality guidelines and toxicity bioassays can be used as complementary tools in sediment quality assessment.

the combined use of sediment chemistry data with toxicity data from elutriate embryo bioassays is a promising approach for integrative assessment of the effects of sediment contamination in coastal systems.
